p:cNvPr.descr: The leftmost alkylating agent structure is S-adenosylmethionine, labeled below. It consists of an adenosine, which is the pentose ring bonded up to a combination 5-sided and 6-sided ring structure. The ring structure has a 5-sided and 6-sided ring component. The apical N on the 5-sided ring double bonds down and right to C, which bonds down to N, which bonds left to C, which bonds up to C, and up and right to the initial N. The 6-sided structure, to the left, has an apical C that bonds up to NH2, double bonds down and left to N, which bonds down to C, which double bonds down and right to N. N bonds up and right to C, which double bonds up to C, which bonds up and left to the initial C. This portion is bracketed below and labeled "adenosine." Below this, the CH2 on the pentose ring bonds left to S+. S+ bonds down to CH3, up to CH2, which bonds up to CH2, which bonds up to C, which bonds left to NH3+, right to H, and up to COO-. This portion is bracketed on the left and labeled "methionene." To the right is a structure labeled "dimethylnitrosamine" below. It consists of O double bonded left to N, which bonds left to N, which bonds up and left and up and right to CH3. To the right is a structure labeled "dimethylsulfate." It consists of an S double bonding up & right and down & right to O, bonding down and left to O which bonds down and left to CH3. S bonds up and left to O, which then bonds up and left to CH3. At the bottom is a structure labeled "nitrogen mustard." It consists of CH3 bonded right to N, which bonds up right and down and right to CH2, which bonds right to CH2, which bonds right to Cl.
